title: Designing Division-by-Zero and Modulo Semantics
description: An evaluator skeleton with TODOs for division-by-zero and remainder behavior. Running it as-is shows unsupported operator errors for `%` and a raw Python `ZeroDivisionError` for `1/0`.

steps.description: AST nodes `Num`, `Var`, `BinOp` with `line` and `col` fields. `LangError` formats messages with the node's location.
`evaluate` handles `Num` and `Var` as before. `Var` uses `difflib` for "did you mean" hints on undefined variables.

`BinOp` evaluates left and right, then has two TODO comments: TODO 1 asks to pick a division-by-zero policy (raise, return `inf`, or return 0). TODO 2 asks to add `%` with consistent zero behavior. The current `ops` dictionary only has `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`.

steps.question: The test cases are `7 % 2`, `7 % 0`, and `1 / 0`. Since `%` is not in `ops`, what happens for the first two?
steps.answer: Both `7 % 2` and `7 % 0` raise `LangError: operator '%' is not supported` with their respective line/column numbers. The division-by-zero case `1 / 0` is in `ops`, so Python executes `left / right` and raises a raw `ZeroDivisionError` without source location.

steps.description: The test loop builds three `BinOp` trees with line/col numbers. Each is evaluated in an empty env. `LangError` is caught and printed with location. `ZeroDivisionError` is caught separately to show the raw Python error that lacks user-source context.
Run it. First test: `7 % 2` at line 1, column 3.
`evaluate` reaches the `ops` check. `%` is not in `ops`. Raises `LangError: operator '%' is not supported (line 1, column 3)`. Caught and printed.
Second test: `7 % 0` at line 2, column 3. Same error: `operator '%' is not supported (line 2, column 3)`. The zero on the right is never checked because `%` fails first.

Third test: `1 / 0` at line 3, column 3. `/` is in `ops`, so the lambda runs. Python raises `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` with no line/col. The `except ZeroDivisionError` block prints `raw Python ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`.
